notes.summary: Blood relation questions describe family links in words, in symbols or by a person "pointing" to someone. The answer is always clear if you draw a small family tree. SSC asks about 1 question in Tier 1 and 1 to 2 in Tier 2. Coded (symbol) questions are the most common in recent papers.

concepts.title: Relation words you must know
concepts.body:
RelationMeans
Grandfather, grandmotherFather or mother of a parent
Paternal uncle (chacha, tau)Father's brother
Paternal aunt (bua)Father's sister
Maternal uncle (mama)Mother's brother
Maternal aunt (mausi)Mother's sister
CousinChild of an uncle or aunt
Nephew, nieceSon, daughter of a brother or sister
Grandson, granddaughterSon, daughter of your child
Father-in-law, mother-in-lawFather, mother of your husband or wife
Brother-in-lawHusband's or wife's brother, or a sister's husband
Sister-in-lawHusband's or wife's sister, or a brother's wife
Son-in-law, daughter-in-lawDaughter's husband, son's wife

concepts.title: Drawing a family tree
concepts.body:
Use one simple notation every time:
  • A square (or +) for a male, a circle (or −) for a female. Use a plain letter if the gender is not known yet.
  • A double line (=) joins a married couple.
  • A single horizontal line joins brothers and sisters.
  • A vertical line goes from parents down to children.
  • Keep each generation on one row: grandparents on top, then parents, then children.
Counting rows tells you the generation gap: one row down is a child, two rows down is a grandchild.

concepts.title: Gender: never assume
concepts.body:
"A is the brother of B" tells you A is male, but says nothing about B. "B is the daughter of C" tells you B is female, but C could be the father or the mother.
So if A is the brother of B, and B is the daughter of C, then C is A's "father or mother". If an option says "cannot be determined" or "father or mother", check carefully whether the gender is really given.
Names in Indian questions usually show gender (Rita, Raj), but do not rely on names when the question uses letters.

concepts.title: Pointing questions: work from "my"
concepts.body:
Break the sentence into small steps, starting from the speaker ("my").
"Pointing to a man, Rita said, 'He is the son of my grandfather's only son.'"
  1. My grandfather's only son = my father.
  2. The son of my father = my brother (or me, but Rita is female).
So the man is Rita's brother.
PhraseUsually means
My father's only son (male speaker)Me
My mother's husbandMy father
My father's wifeMy mother
My grandfather's only sonMy father
My grandmother's only childMy father or my mother
My father's brother's sonMy cousin
My wife's father's only daughterMy wife

concepts.title: Coded relations
concepts.body:
Symbols stand for relations, for example: A + B means A is the father of B; A − B means A is the wife of B; A × B means A is the brother of B; A ÷ B means A is the daughter of B.
  1. Write each symbol's meaning in a small table first.
  2. Read the expression two letters at a time from left to right: in P + Q × R, first "P is the father of Q", then "Q is the brother of R".
  3. Draw each link on the tree as you read it, marking genders.
  4. Read off the asked relation.
For "which expression shows that Q is the son of P", test each option the same way and stop when one gives the exact relation (including gender).

concepts.title: Generations and family puzzles
concepts.body:
In larger puzzles (six or eight members, "two married couples"), list every fact, then:
  1. Place couples first; they share a row.
  2. Place parents above children.
  3. Fill genders from words like husband, wife, son, daughter, brother, sister.
  4. Answer counting questions (how many males, how many couples) only after every person is on the tree.
Generation check: "grand-" words are two rows apart; parent and child, uncle and nephew are one row apart; brothers, sisters, cousins and couples are on the same row.

concepts.title: Common mistakes and quick checks
concepts.body:
• Direction of the relation: "A is the father of B" is not "B is the father of A". Always read who is related to whom in the question ("How is A related to B?" means describe A).
  • In-laws: a brother's wife is a sister-in-law; a sister's husband is a brother-in-law.
  • Mother's side or father's side: maternal means mother's side; paternal means father's side.
  • When two answers seem possible, check the gender of the person asked about.

varieties.name: Pointing and introducing
varieties.how: Start from "my" and simplify the phrase one step at a time, replacing each part with a single relation. Then relate the result to the speaker.

example.q: Pointing to a girl, Aryan said, "She is the daughter of the only child of my grandmother." How is the girl related to Aryan?
steps: The only child of my grandmother is my father or my mother: Aryan's parent.
The daughter of Aryan's parent is Aryan's sister.

varieties.name: Direct statements
varieties.how: Draw each statement on the tree as you read it, with genders. Then read the relation between the two asked people.

example.q: Vinita and Amita are the sisters of Gaurav. Ashish is the father of Vinita. Ansh is the son of Amita. How is Ashish related to Ansh?
steps: Vinita, Amita and Gaurav are siblings, so Ashish is the father of all three, including Amita.
Ashish is the father of Ansh's mother.

varieties.name: Coded relations
varieties.how: Write the meaning of each symbol. Read the expression two letters at a time, draw each link with gender, then read off the asked relation.

example.q: A @ B means A is the daughter of B; A & B means A is the husband of B; A % B means A is the wife of B. If D @ N @ H & Y @ F % V, how is N related to F?
steps: N @ H: N is the daughter of H.
H & Y: H is the husband of Y, so Y is N's mother.
Y @ F: Y is the daughter of F.
So N is the daughter of F's daughter.

varieties.name: Family puzzle
varieties.how: Place couples on the same row and children below them. Mark every gender you can. Answer only after all members are placed.

example.q: P is the husband of Q. R and S are the children of Q. T is the wife of R. U is the son of T. S is an unmarried girl. How many female members are there?
steps: Q is a wife, so female. T is a wife, so female. S is a girl.
P is a husband, R is T's husband (male), U is a son (male).

tips: Always draw the tree; even a 10-second sketch avoids most mistakes.
Mark gender only when the question tells you. "Brother of B" says nothing about B.
In pointing questions, start from "my" and simplify step by step.
In coded questions, write the symbol table first and read two letters at a time.
Keep generations on separate rows; "grand" relations are two rows apart.
Check the direction asked: "How is A related to B" means describe A from B's side.
traps: Assuming the gender of a person from a relation that only describes someone else.
Reversing the relation (answering "son" when the question asks how the father is related).
Mixing maternal and paternal: a mother's brother is a maternal uncle.
In coded questions, forgetting that "A − B: A is the wife of B" also tells you B is male.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Rita said, "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is the man related to Rita?
questions.solution:
Rita's grandfather's only son = Rita's father.
The son of Rita's father = Rita's brother.

questions.q: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. How is C related to A?
questions.solution:
B is the daughter of C, so C is B's parent.
A is B's brother, so C is also A's parent.
C's gender is not given, so C is A's father or mother.

questions.q:
P + Q means P is the father of Q; P − Q means P is the wife of Q; P × Q means P is the brother of Q; P ÷ Q means P is the daughter of Q.
If A + B × C − D, how is D related to A?
questions.solution:
A + B: A is the father of B.
B × C: B is the brother of C, so C is also A's child.
C − D: C is the wife of D, so C is A's daughter.
D is the husband of A's daughter = A's son-in-law.

questions.q: Introducing a woman, Raj said, "She is the wife of the only son of my father." How is the woman related to Raj?
questions.solution:
The only son of Raj's father is Raj himself.
So the woman is Raj's wife.

questions.q: In a family, P is the father of Q. Q is the mother of R and S. R is a boy and S is a girl. T is the brother of P. U is the wife of P. How is S related to U?
questions.solution:
U is the wife of P, and P is the father of Q, so Q is U's child.
S is Q's child, so S is U's grandchild.
S is a girl, so S is U's granddaughter.

questions.q:
A @ B means A is the mother of B; A # B means A is the husband of B; A $ B means A is the daughter of B; A % B means A is the brother of B.
If M % N @ O # P $ Q, how is M related to O?
questions.solution:
M % N: M is the brother of N.
N @ O: N is the mother of O.
So M is the brother of O's mother = O's maternal uncle.
(O # P $ Q only tells us about O's wife P and her parent Q.)
